text: Access reviews and least privilege — granting exactly what's needed, and nothing more.

An engineer gets temporary prod access to help an incident. The incident resolves, but nobody revokes the grant. A year later, ten more grants like it exist — each reasonable at the time, collectively excessive now.
Every quarter, list every write and admin grant. Ask if this person still needs it right now. Revoke anything the answer is no or not sure to — the same recurring pattern as right-sizing capacity.
Masking controls who sees sensitive values. Secrets management protects specific credentials. Access reviews protect the broader accounts that could bypass or request either one.
None of Chapter 3's security lessons fully works without this recurring check behind it. Next up: capacity planning — looking ahead, not just reacting.
